result.title: Dynamic Interpolation for Training-Time Prediction Reshaping in Low-Light Image Enhancement
result.comment: 18 pages, 9 figures. Published in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology (Early Access)
result.summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) is an important image/video processing problem for reliable visual systems under poor illumination, yet it remains challenging due to the strong coupling among insufficient illumination, noise amplification, and structural degradation. Existing methods typically rely on sophisticated network architectures or engineered objective functions. While effective, the former increases model complexity and deployment burden, whereas the latter relies on empirically tuned loss weights. We revisit supervised LLIE from a training-dynamics perspective and observe that brightness-related errors tend to converge early, while residual noise and structural artifacts often remain insufficiently optimized in later stages. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic Interpolation Training-only Module (DITM), which introduces no additional learnable parameters and adaptively reshapes the model prediction for supervised feed-forward LLIE training. Specifically, DITM employs brightness-aware interpolation, in which the model prediction is combined with a mean brightness-aligned image constructed by rescaling the model prediction according to the mean brightness of the ground-truth image. By reducing the relative dominance of global brightness discrepancy, DITM makes residual local errors more influential during backpropagation after global luminance has largely stabilized, thereby facilitating artifact suppression and fine-detail restoration in later training stages. DITM is used only during training and is fully removed at inference, introducing no additional inference cost. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets and CNN-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based LLIE backbones show that DITM consistently improves fidelity and perceptual quality while preserving the inference-time architecture and introducing no additional inference-time computation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从训练动力学角度重新审视有监督低光图像增强，指出亮度相关误差收敛过早、残差噪声与结构伪影后期优化不足，提出无需额外参数、仅训练期生效的动态插值模块 DITM：将模型预测与按真值平均亮度重标定得到的图像插值，削弱全局亮度差异的主导地位，使局部残差误差在后期反传中更受重视，推理时完全移除。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「训练期重塑预测以改变不同误差项在反传中主导性」的做法，可能为 latent 轨迹训练中答案损失与视觉监督的贡献分配、分阶段监督权重设计提供可核查线索，虽属像素级增强任务，但机制本身与推理状态无直接关系。
